description: Direct event setup on the built-in jira_dc source, with the Bitbucket Data Center repository picked from the user's connection and stored as its clone URL. The create body validates against CreatePromptAutomationRequest in OpenHands/automation (openhands/automation/preset_router.py).

scenarios.description: A picked repository, project key, the default label and a Jira token secret name, on a service whose runs do not clone Bitbucket Data Center: no repos, the prompt has the agent clone the repository with the owner's connection. Preflight passes, the automation is created.

draft.name: Jira Data Center issue to Bitbucket Data Center PR - https://bitbucket.example.com/scm/ENG/payments.git
draft.prompt:
A Jira Data Center issue in project ENG was labelled 'openhands'. Its key, summary, description and comments are in the event payload below. Implement what it asks in the Bitbucket Data Center repository https://bitbucket.example.com/scm/ENG/payments.git.

1. Unless the repository is already cloned in the workspace, clone it with the Bitbucket Data Center token you receive as the bitbucket_data_center_token secret (use the bitbucket-data-center skill for the clone URL and authentication).
2. Create a branch named after the issue key, for example openhands/ENG-123. Never push to the default branch, and change no other repository.
3. Implement the change and run the repository's relevant tests and checks.
4. Push the branch and open a pull request in that repository through the Bitbucket Data Center REST API, titled with the issue key and summary, and describing the change and the test results.
5. Jira token secret name: 'JIRA_DC_TOKEN'. If that name is not empty and the secret is available, add a comment with the pull request link to the issue through the Jira Data Center REST API, at the base URL of the issue's `self` link. Otherwise skip this step.

If the issue does not contain enough information to implement it, open no pull request and explain what is missing in your final message, and in the Jira comment when a token is configured.

trigger.filter: issue.fields.project.key == 'ENG' && ((webhookEvent == 'jira:issue_created' && contains(issue.fields.labels || `[]`, 'openhands')) || (webhookEvent == 'jira:issue_updated' && length(changelog.items[?field == 'labels' && contains(join('', [' ', to_string(toString), ' ']), ' openhands ') && !contains(join('', [' ', to_string(fromString), ' ']), ' openhands ')] || `[]`) > `0`))
